What We Do

Full-Service Allergy / Immunology Revenue Cycle Management

Allergy and immunology billing is driven by high-volume testing codes, recurring immunotherapy dose billing, and biologic drug prior authorization. PMEX manages every layer, from initial allergy testing through years of immunotherapy maintenance doses, inside your existing EHR workflow.

Allergy Skin Testing

Percutaneous (95004) and intradermal (95024) testing coded per allergen count.

Immunotherapy Billing

Single-dose (95115) and multi-dose (95117) injection billing every visit.

Patch Testing

95044 coded per allergen series with correct date-of-read billing.

Biologic Prior Authorization

Dupilumab, omalizumab, mepolizumab auth managed cycle-to-cycle.

Pulmonary Function Testing

Spirometry (94010) and full PFT panels billed separately from E/M.

Telehealth A&I Billing

Modifier 95 applied with payer-specific allergy telehealth rules.

Sound Familiar?

Common Allergy / Immunology Billing Problems, and How PMEX Fixes Them

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Immunotherapy dose count submitted wrong, fewer doses billed than administered.

PMEX counts administered doses from the injection record, not the vial, on every visit.

Allergy testing units undercounted, percutaneous series not fully coded.

PMEX codes the full allergen count from the testing record before every submission.

Biologic prior auth expires between cycles, claim denied mid-treatment.

PMEX tracks biologic auth expirations 14 days ahead and initiates renewal automatically.

Patch test read billed on wrong date, Day 2 and Day 4 reads bundled incorrectly.

PMEX bills each patch test read as a separate service with the correct date of service.

Immunotherapy serum preparation (95165) never billed, only injections submitted.

PMEX submits 95165 serum preparation alongside injection codes on qualifying visits.

Spirometry denied, not linked to the qualifying diagnosis on the same claim.

PMEX confirms diagnosis code linkage before submitting spirometry with the E/M.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Allergy Billing, and How PMEX Fixes Them

Allergy practices lose 14–22% of revenue to preventable denials. These three patterns account for over 60% of A&I claim failures.

PATTERN 01

Immunotherapy Dose Count Error

Multi-dose visit: 3 doses administered. 95117 billed as 1 unit instead of 3. $85 per visit lost across every multi-dose patient.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX counts administered doses from the injection nursing log, not the prescription, and bills 95115 or 95117 per the actual count documented every visit.

PATTERN 02

Biologic Authorization Expired, Claim Denied Retroactively

Omalizumab dose administered. Commercial auth expired 2 days prior. No one flagged the renewal. $1,100 drug + $250 admin denied retroactively.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks biologic auth expiration 14 days ahead and initiates renewal with treatment response documentation before the next scheduled dose.

PATTERN 03

Allergy Testing Bundled with E/M Incorrectly

New patient evaluation with 20-allergen percutaneous panel. Testing codes (95004 x20) not submitted, team assumed bundled. $220 in testing revenue lost on the first visit.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX submits allergy testing codes separately from the E/M on every first-visit evaluation, applying modifier -25 and billing the full allergen count.
